items.author: RedLetterMedia
items.content: <article>Mystery Men is a 1999 comedy with a big budget and an all-star cast that flopped hard. items.title: The Decade Hollywood Stopped Saying No
items.author: FilmStack
items.content:
<article>When Hollywood felt the pressure, they panicked. And what did they do? They gave a generation of directors more control than ever before. That decision sent shockwaves through the film industry and resulted in one of the biggest transformative periods in Hollywood. This was the 1970s and we are still living with the effects from this time period.

Some of the biggest directors ever shined during this time. Steven Spielberg, George Lucas, Francis Ford Coppola, Robert Altman, Martin Scorsese, and more. These directors evolved the film industry more than any others. From Jaws to Star Wars to Apocalypse Now to The Exorcist, this video covers the 1970s like no other video.

This is a story of when Hollywood lost it's way, then lost control, then took that control back, all because of the same reasons.

Chapters:
00:00 - Intro
01:10 - Act 1: Hollywood Loses Control
05:40 - Act 2: The Filmmakers Take Over
12:47 - Act 3: The New Formula

items.title: RON HOWARD - Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 210 Ron Howard - Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with director Ron Howard (AVEDON, APOLLO 13, A BEAUTIFUL MIND). Ron has worked professionally in film and television since the age of 4, and he reflects on his life and career throughout the episode, from chewing fake glass with Yul Brenner as a child actor to directing a wide variety of features and documentaries for almost 50 years. A graduate of the Roger Corman movie factory, Ron reveals what he learned about leadership and collaboration while directing GRAND THEFT AUTO, his directorial debut, under Roger's guidance, and we discuss whether any modern equivalent exists for filmmakers today as a proving ground. Ron also shares how he pushed himself early on to always be creating, and we discuss the creation of several of his films and what he aims for in every movie he makes. We later ask what draws him to a potential project, and we discuss his foray into directing documentaries and how it differs from shooting fiction. We worked with Ron on A BEAUTIFUL MIND, and we had a wonderful time catching up with him.

This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠

items.title: ROBIN SWICORD - Writer / Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 209 Robin Swicord - Writer / Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director Robin Swicord (WAKEFIELD, WHEN THEY SEE US, PRACTICAL MAGIC). Throughout the episode, Robin is frank about her experience working in the film industry as a woman, and we discuss how she's seen the culture and behaviour within the industry change over the years. Robin wrote the script for the 1994 adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN, and she shares what it took for the studio to finally greenlight the film after 12 years of development. She also reflects on the long development process of BENJAMIN BUTTON, and she reveals what her initial vision for the story was. After years as a writer, Robin was able to direct her first feature, THE JANE AUSTEN BOOK CLUB, and she shares how she cast the film on short notice and how she prepped for it as a first-time director. We later discuss how she shot her second film as a director, WAKEFIELD, in just 18 days, and she reflects on what she brought from her experiences on her first film to the second one.

This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠

items.title: JOHN LEE HANCOCK - Writer / Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 208 John Lee Hancock - Writer / Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director John Lee Hancock (THE HIGHWAYMEN, THE ROOKIE, A PERFECT WORLD). John was born and raised in Texas and we learn how he made the transition from practicing law to screenwriting and what he stayed busy with to survive in Los Angeles after moving there. John later reflects on learning filmmaking from Clint Eastwood and Kevin Costner during the production of A PERFECT WORLD (which John wrote), and he reveals how he came up with the idea of the film. We also learn how producer Mark Johnson (Season 2, Episode 97) accidentally set him up to direct his first film, and John reveals some of the benefits of being a writer while also working as a director. John also reflects on the grand-scaled production of THE ALAMO, and we discuss the historical and cultural backdrop of Texas at the time of the events of the movie. Towards the end, John shares some information with us about his next film, and we discuss the economic difficulties of filming within the United States that lead to productions shooting abroad.

Recommended Viewing: A PERFECT WORLD

The filmmaker looks back on seeing DR. STRANGELOVE in the cinema with his parents as a teenager, talks about a failed attempt to show one of his favorite movies to Robert Crumb, and shares how ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER inspired the look of GHOST WORLD.

The Picks:
DR. STRANGELOVE, OR: HOW I LEARNED TO STOP WORRYING AND LOVE THE BOMB (Stanley Kubrick, 1964)
THE KILLERS (Robert Siodmak, 1946)
ARMY OF SHADOWS (Jean-Pierre Melville, 1969)
THE ASPHALT JUNGLE (John Huston, 1950)
ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER (Pedro Almodóvar, 1999)
